text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Extra wage rises of up to 40 percent for civil servants will take 145 trillion lira out of the budget.
- Foreign Minister and coalition partner Tansu Ciller vows to step down if she does not make Turkey a fully European nation and unite the fractious Turkish right.
- Turkish business circles welcome statement from European Union foreign ministers that leaves the door open for Turkish membership of the EU.
- Leading member of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party criticises bid to crack down on Islamic dress.
- The governor of Ankara closes three illegal Koran courses in clamp down on Islamist activism.
- President Suleyman Demirel says that 13,000 of the 72,000 villages in Turkey have no running water.
- Turkish businessmen who had invested in Albania say they will return there as soon as the current crisis is over.
- Turkey plans to sell F-5 jets to the Philippines.
